newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest should be frost-free next two weeks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest should be frost-free next two weeks.

text.p: Meteorologists said weather maps suggest the U.S. Midwest will be frost-free through the end of the month, while temperatures should range from slightly above normal this week to slightly below normal next week.

"During the next 10 days, I see little if any chance of any major surges of cold air moving down into the Midwest," said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis in his daily report. "In fact, the chances of any frost/freeze damage from now through the end of the month are remote at best."

High temperatures this week should range from the mid 60s to mid 70 degrees Fahrenheit, with lows from the upper 40s to upper 50s. Next week the western Midwest should cool with highs in the 60s, while in the eastern Midwest highs should be from the mid 60s to mid 70s.

The Midwest should be mostly dry through Thursday, with light rain likely in the western Midwest Friday and Saturday. More scattered showers were likely Monday and Tuesday across much of the Midwest, said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc.
The southern Midwest received 0.5 to two inches of rain the past 48 hours as remnants of Hurricane Fausto moved east across the U.S. Midwest, said Gesser.
The southern third of Illinois received 0.5 to 1.50 inches since Sunday. Since Monday the southern half of Indiana and Ohio received one to two inches.
Gesser said the rains could delay corn harvest, which was under way in southern Illinois and Indiana.
